transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. I came in because... well, I've been having this issue lately. After my late shifts, I'll stop for food, but then I just keep going once I get home. I'll eat a full takeout meal, and then I'll move on to chips, sweets, just whatever is in the apartment, really. And afterward, I'm honestly kind of shocked by how much I actually ate. It's been bothering me, so I figured I should probably talk to someone about it.
After these episodes of eating, do you ever feel the need to do something to get rid of the calories, such as vomiting, using laxatives, or exercising excessively?

Yeah, I do. Um, sometimes after I get home and eat way too much of that takeout or all those snacks, I'll go to the bathroom and make myself throw up. I just... I don't want all that food to just sit in me and turn into extra weight. So, yeah, that's what I do to get rid of it.

latest_inference.note: The patient's admission of compensatory behaviors (self-induced vomiting) following episodes of binge eating shifts the diagnosis from binge eating disorder to bulimia nervosa.
